title: GAP Waiver Addenda and Other Products on the Same Contract
content:
This policy covers how GAP Waiver Addenda relate to the other records of the borrower and of the contract.

1. **Own contract only.** A benefit is computed from the records of the addendum's own contract only. Losses, balances and refunds of the borrower's other contracts are never combined with it.
2. **Vehicle service contract on the same contract.** Holding a vehicle service contract on the same contract changes the benefit. On a total loss the service contract is cancelled. Its unearned refund, as computed under the service-contract refund rules on the date of loss, is an excluded amount that reduces the GAP benefit whether or not the refund has been issued yet; the same applies to any other cancellable add-on product financed in the contract. **The clause making that unearned refund an excluded amount is no longer in force on a GAP Waiver Premier 150 claim or a GAP Waiver Plus 150 claim**, where the current exclusion basis of each of those plans governs the service contract's refund. On a claim on any other plan, the unearned refund, as computed under the service-contract refund rules on the date of loss, is still an excluded amount whether or not it has been issued. The cancellation of the service contract on a total loss stays in force for every plan.
3. **Force-placed insurance.** Force-placed insurance never counts as the borrower's primary insurance. Premiums it added to the contract balance are excluded amounts. **The clause making those premiums excluded amounts is no longer in force on a GAP Waiver Premier 150 claim or a GAP Waiver Plus 150 claim**, where the current exclusion basis of each of those plans governs the force-placed premiums. On a claim on any other plan, every premium force-placed insurance added to the contract balance is still an excluded amount. The rule that force-placed insurance is never primary insurance stays in force for every plan.
4. **Independent cancellation.** An addendum and a service contract on the same contract are cancelled and refunded independently, each under its own rules.

| Question | Answer under this policy |
|---|---|
| Can a loss on a borrower's second contract affect the benefit on the first? | No. Only the addendum's own contract counts. |
| Does force-placed coverage satisfy the primary insurance requirement? | No, never. |
| Does cancelling the service contract cancel the addendum? | No. Each is cancelled and refunded under its own rules. |
